statement: Sketch the graph of $y=x^3-3x$, and find the coordinates of its stationary points.
solution:
Differentiating, $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=3x^2-3=3(x-1)(x+1)$, so the stationary points are at $x=1$ and $x=-1$.

At $x=1$, $y=1-3=-2$; at $x=-1$, $y=-1+3=2$. So the stationary points are $(1,-2)$ (a local minimum) and $(-1,2)$ (a local maximum).

The curve passes through the origin and has roots at $x=-\sqrt3,0,\sqrt3$. As $x\to\infty$, $y\to\infty$; as $x\to-\infty$, $y\to-\infty$. The graph rises to $(-1,2)$, falls to $(1,-2)$, then rises again.
hints: Substitute back for y and use the shape of a cubic.
